h1: The 5 Best KVM Docking Stations for Two Computers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best KVM Docking Stations 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five KVM docking stations that share monitors, keyboard and mouse between two computers, compared on power, ports and resolution.
summary: The AV Access 100W KVM dock is the best KVM docking station for two computers: two monitors, two laptops and a rated 100W of power delivery for each, with EDID emulation, for $100 to $200. The 13-in-1 dock has the widest port selection, the 60W AV Access runs fast 2K monitors, and the UGREEN shares three monitors cheaply.
intro: The usual two-computer desk mistake is buying a good dock and a separate KVM switch, then finding the cables are a tangle and one laptop still will not charge. A KVM dock merges both jobs: it switches your keyboard, mouse and monitors between machines while delivering power to whichever laptop is active. The spec that decides daily use is watts per computer, not the number of ports.

We reviewed five units on paper, comparing power delivery per computer, monitor count and resolution, and port selection. We ranked on spec sheets and owner reports, not bench testing, and show price in buckets. We dropped plain docks that need a separate KVM, since they do not fit the title. Watts, refresh rate and input type separate the five.

products.name: AV Access Docking Station KVM Switch 2 Monitors 2 Laptops (100W)
products.verdict: The most power per laptop at a reasonable price.
products.description:
This AV Access dock shares two monitors between two laptops and is rated for 100W power delivery to each PC, with 1G Ethernet and EDID emulation. It supports 4K on dual monitors and sells for $100 to $200. A 100W rating is enough to charge most performance laptops while they work, so one cable covers video, data and power.

It ranks first because 100W suits most performance laptops, while the 60W AV Access model below it charges more slowly and costs more. It gives up the 8K ceiling of the AV Access 8K. EDID emulation keeps windows from rearranging when you switch computers.

It suits a home office with two work laptops. The caveat is that the 100W figure is a rating, so a power-hungry laptop under load may still draw more. Skip it if you need 8K or a third monitor.
products.idealFor: Two work laptops sharing two monitors.
products.skipIf: You need 8K or a third monitor.

products.name: KVM Switch 2 Monitors 2 Computers Docking Station (13-in-1)
products.verdict: The widest port selection and high refresh outputs.
products.description:
This aluminum 13-in-1 dock takes USB-C plus HDMI and DisplayPort inputs, delivers 100W and outputs 4K at 60Hz or 4K at 120Hz on two monitors. It sells for $100 to $200. HDMI and DisplayPort inputs mean a desktop can join the setup alongside a laptop, which a USB-C-only dock cannot offer.

It ranks second because those inputs let a desktop join a laptop, which the 100W AV Access focuses less on. The tradeoff is an unfamiliar brand name against AV Access. Against the AV Access 8K, it adds charging, while the 8K model raises the resolution ceiling.

It suits buyers with mixed devices who need many ports. The caveat is that high refresh rates depend on the right cables and monitors. Skip it if you only run two USB-C laptops.
products.idealFor: Mixed laptop and desktop users needing many ports.
products.skipIf: You only run two USB-C laptops.

products.name: AV Access KVM Switch Dock 2 Monitors 2 Laptops
products.verdict: Fast refresh rates, but only 60W per laptop.
products.description:
This AV Access dock connects two monitors and two laptops over two USB-C MST ports, with 60W power delivery to each PC, 1G Ethernet and EDID emulation. It handles up to 2K at 144Hz or 1080p at 240Hz and sells for $200 to $500. MST, multi-stream transport, splits one USB-C link across two displays.

It ranks third because the 100W AV Access charges faster for less. Its edge is the high refresh output for gaming or smooth scrolling. Against the 13-in-1, it offers lower power and fewer ports but a tested 144Hz figure.

It suits users with fast 2K monitors. The caveat is 60W, which may leave a large laptop under-powered. Skip it if your laptop needs more than 60W.
products.idealFor: People with fast 2K monitors and efficient laptops.

products.name: AV Access 8K KVM Switch 2 Monitors 2 Computers
products.verdict: Headroom for very high resolution and mixed computers.
products.description:
This AV Access switch supports up to 8K resolution across two monitors and two computers, works with laptop and desktop combinations and includes GbE networking. It sells for $200 to $500. Eight-K support is mostly headroom today, but a switch that passes it will not become the bottleneck when you upgrade your monitors.

It ranks fourth because the specs do not list power delivery, which the two docks above highlight. You buy it for resolution headroom and desktop compatibility. Against the 100W dock, it is the better choice only if your monitors demand more pixels.

It suits owners of a high-resolution monitor or a laptop and desktop pair. The caveat is that you should confirm charging separately. Skip it if you need the dock to charge your laptop.
products.idealFor: High-resolution monitors and mixed computer setups.
products.skipIf: You need the dock to charge your laptop.

products.name: UGREEN 8K@60Hz KVM Switch 3 Monitors 2 Computers
products.verdict: A cheap way to share three monitors.
products.description:
The UGREEN switch shares three monitors between two computers, supports 8K at 60Hz or 4K at 240Hz and has an aluminum case and four USB 3.0 ports. The box includes four DisplayPort cables, two HDMI cables, a power adapter and a controller. It sells for $50 to $100. Cables in the box save a purchase, since the wrong cable is the usual cause of a black screen.

It closes the list because it is a KVM switch, not a full dock, so no charging or Ethernet is listed. It wins on monitor count and bundled cables. Against the AV Access 8K, it costs less and adds a third monitor.

It suits triple-monitor desks on a budget. The caveat is that you will need a separate way to charge laptops. Skip it if you want one cable to charge and connect.
products.idealFor: Triple-monitor desks on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You want one cable to charge and connect.

methodology.title: Power delivery
methodology.description: Per-computer wattage was weighed since a dock that cannot charge a laptop defeats the point.

whatMatters.detail: Power delivery is the wattage a dock sends to charge your laptop. A laptop that needs 90W but gets 60W will charge slowly or drain under load. Match the listed wattage to your charger rating. The AV Access and 13-in-1 list 100W, the second AV Access 60W, and the UGREEN and AV Access 8K list none, so assume those do not charge. Add a separate charger for any laptop that needs one.

Resolution and refresh rate describe sharpness and smoothness, and docks often cap them when two monitors run at once. A dock listing 4K at 120Hz may only do so with specific cables. Read the exact combination in the listing, as the 13-in-1 lists 4K60 or 4K120 and the AV Access 2K at 144Hz. Dual 4K at high refresh often needs the best cables and ports on both ends.

EDID emulation keeps a monitor's settings steady when you switch computers, so windows do not jump around. Without it, desktops can rearrange and icons scramble. Look for the term in the spec list. The AV Access units list it, and it saves time every time you switch machines.

USB-C inputs suit laptops, while HDMI and DisplayPort suit desktops. A dock with only USB-C cannot take a tower. Check the input list against both of your computers. The 13-in-1 and AV Access 8K list desktop inputs, while the two AV Access docks are laptop focused. Mixed setups, such as a laptop and a tower, need the broader input list.

A dock adds Ethernet, USB and charging, while a plain KVM only switches. A dock reduces cable clutter. Read whether the listing says docking station or KVM switch. The UGREEN is a switch with no charging, while the AV Access models are docks.

faq.q: Can a KVM dock charge two laptops at once?
faq.a: These units power the active laptop, and listings quote wattage per PC. Check the figure against your charger, since the AV Access 100W and 13-in-1 list 100W and the other AV Access 60W.

Buying a dock without enough wattage. Under-power makes laptops charge slowly. Match each laptop's charger rating to the dock, especially for performance machines. A mismatch shows up as a laptop that charges slowly or drains while you work.

faq.q: Is the 8K model worth it over the 100W dock?
faq.a: Only if you have an 8K monitor or a desktop to share. Otherwise the 100W dock does more, because it charges both laptops and costs less. An 8K monitor is rare, so most buyers pay for headroom they never use.

Yes, high resolutions need the right HDMI or DisplayPort cables. The UGREEN includes several. Check cable ratings before you blame the dock for a missing signal. A DisplayPort 1.4 cable is the usual fix for high refresh.

faq.q: Will my windows rearrange when I switch?
faq.a: EDID emulation helps prevent that. The AV Access units list it, so they keep monitor arrangements stable. Cheaper switches without it can scramble layouts. After switching, give the monitors a second to settle before moving windows. If layouts still jump, reboot the dock once.

faq.q: Can I use this with a desktop?
faq.a: The 13-in-1 and AV Access 8K list desktop-friendly inputs. The USB-C units are laptop focused, so check the input list before pairing a tower. A desktop may also need its own power for the switch.

finalTake: Buy the AV Access 100W dock for two work laptops sharing two monitors. Choose the 13-in-1 for a laptop and desktop mix, the 60W AV Access model for fast 2K monitors, and the AV Access 8K for very high resolution. The UGREEN is a switch for three monitors on a budget. Match the wattage to each laptop's charger before you buy.
